correctness.rationale: The greedy completing letters give an absent subsequence when there are too few arches. A prefix before the kth arch has exact completion deficit q(k-r)-s, so when slack is zero only missing symbols are feasible; with positive slack all are feasible. The ordered missing-symbol list and its LIFO undo preserve lexicographic child order without inspecting forbidden letters. Between complete outputs the DFS uses at most two monotone depth segments, with O(1) work per edge except at arch resets. Each reset can be charged to q letters on a path, and at most k<=n/q lists coexist; writing the word fits the O(n) bound. The k=0, q=1, n=0 and empty-family branches are consistent. The constant-time infeasibility test can compare k with floor(n/q) to avoid a large product.
residual_risks: The O(n) through-last-output phrase is read within its zero/one-output context, not as total time for a family with many outputs. Bounds concern the stated word RAM and explicit materialization. The supplied large-case tests check membership, not independently the precise ranks of the first three words.

value.rationale: This resolves a stated enumeration-delay question, reaching the linear cost of materializing a word even over growing alphabets. The simultaneous linear initialization for feasible positive k and linear memory make the result useful in the intended streaming setting; it is not a fixed-q rephrasing or an amortized-only bound.
residual_risks: The optimality claim depends on explicit output; it does not compare succinct encodings or ranking/unranking capabilities.
